summary: Replace the blank-next placeholder with a playable third-person Shield Wall tactics game: wobbly jointed-skeleton captains and bots, formation scrolls, four-fort domination with currency-bought units and defenses, then local and networked multiplayer.
understanding: Problem: Build a third-person squad-tactics game blending Shieldwall formation combat with Fall Guys wobbly ragdoll movement, where a Captain fights in person and commands swordsmen and archer bots on a four-fort domination map. Solution: Ship the locked five-phase loop — jointed-skeleton spring-damper wobble; visually distinct bots; cone-detected combat with projectile arrows, melee hit-trace, and force thresholds (under 20 stumble, 20–50 knockdown, over 50 death); a real-time formation scroll plus a view-only map scroll; currency-bought mix of up to 20 units versus castle defenses; capture via scaling walls or breaking doors; medieval gear rewards; 20-second fort respawns at full health; captain-death retreat; replication-friendly local multiplayer then real networked play. Out of scope: first-person camera, blood/gore, unique Captain combat abilities, pausing time in the scroll, click-ordering from the map, a bean-only physics prototype, and a bot spawn invulnerability window.
decompositionStrategy: This is a net-new product on the blank-next Next.js 15 foundation (no Unreal project, no C++ toolchain, no test runner, placeholder `/`). The locked Unreal/C++/Chaos/GAS decisions are implemented as a TypeScript authoritative simulation plus a Three.js third-person view so the game is actually playable at `/play` and testable with vitest. Ticket 001 is the walking skeleton (landing rewrite, sim engine, snapshot protocol, spring-damper ragdoll, `/play`) because that plumbing is unproven here. Later tickets register systems and data tables into that engine rather than rewriting it. 002 owns unit appearance and roam; 003 owns GAS/combat/hit reactions; 004 owns command/scrolls/sensors; 005 owns world/economy/capture/lifecycle; 006 owns AI kings and match victory; 007 owns the net transport (local multi-captain host plus a real WebSocket match server). `lib/game/sim/**` and `app/(game)/play/page.tsx` stay 001-owned shared touchpoints. No two delivery tickets own the same path.

tasks.title: Ship landing page and wobbly physics prototype
tasks.goal: Replace the synthesized blank-next home with a Shield Wall product landing, add a /play third-person battlefield, and land the authoritative TypeScript simulation that walks a single jointed-skeleton Captain (cylinder/capsule limbs, spring-damper joints, active balance). When this ticket is done an operator can open /, click into /play, walk the wobbly Captain with WASD + mouse, and fire debug impulses that classify as stumble / knockdown / death at the locked force thresholds.
acceptanceCriteria: app/page.tsx does not exist and app/(game)/page.tsx exists, so Next has a single / route
GET / response body contains the exact string Shield Wall and the exact string Enter the field
GET /play returns HTTP 200 and the response body contains Shield Wall battlefield
pnpm test -- lib/game exits 0

classifyHitForce(19) returns 'stumble', classifyHitForce(20) returns 'knockdown', classifyHitForce(50) returns 'knockdown', classifyHitForce(51) returns 'death' (unit test in lib/game/data/hit-reactions.test.ts)

tasks.title: Build forts, economy, capture, and respawn
tasks.goal: Stand up the four-corner domination world: moderate terrain (forests, one river, central hill), forts with purchasable walls and gates, starting cash that can buy a full 20-unit army or a mix of units and defenses, medieval capture gear, physical shield upgrades, 20-second full-health fort respawns, and captain-death retreat. When this ticket is done a player can spend a treasury, garrison a fort, break or scale an enemy gate/wall (or walk in if the owner bought no defenses), capture it, and watch dead bots walk back from the home gate after 20 seconds.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/game/data/economy.ts exports STARTING_TREASURY === 2000, UNIT_COST === 100, and MAX_SQUAD_SIZE usage such that STARTING_TREASURY / UNIT_COST === 20
tryRecruit of 20 swordsmen on a fresh treasury succeeds and leaves treasury === 0; a 21st recruit returns error: 'squad_cap' or error: 'cannot_afford'
tryBuyDefense('high_wall') on a treasury that already bought 20 units returns error: 'cannot_afford'; on a fresh treasury it succeeds and fort.defense.wall === 'high'

A unit entering a wall === 'none' and gate === 'none' courtyard with no living enemies flips fort.ownerTeamId to that unit's team; a gate === 'wood' blocks entry until gate.hp <= 0 (lib/game/world/capture.test.ts)

applyHit on a shield-upgraded unit from the front at sword force does not set hitReaction.state to death and records blockedBy === 'shield'; the same hit from behind applies the full force band (lib/game/economy/shield.test.ts)

A dead bot reaches hitReaction.state === 'alive' (or equivalent not-dead) at tick 1200 after death, at the home fort spawn, with health === maxHealth, and has no State.Invulnerable tag; by tick 1500 its XZ is closer to its last ordered slot than it was at respawn (lib/game/lifecycle/respawn.test.ts)
On captain death, every living allied bot has order.mode === 'retreat' and a visible shout payload Retreat! (lib/game/lifecycle/captain-death.test.ts)
